title: The pre-commit reseal holds a proof whose closure the commit does not carry, before running it
intention: The pre-commit reseal runs a proof only when the commit carries everything the proof measures, so a seal and any trouble it raises describe the tree being committed, never uncommitted work beside it.
why: The BUILDME-records commit 4faf4e29 (11cd253f10bc) staged only cairn/tools/base records, and the pre-commit reseal ran every cairn/tools/base proof over the working tree carrying 11cd's uncommitted transitions.py: test_transitions.py ran red, raised seal-red-cairn-tools-base, and 22 base validations were held. A seal and a trouble must describe the tree being committed. Asked for by the peer's foreground call F17 (b) (/home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md line 458), Akien's to overturn.
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — a seal must measure the bytes it is a claim about) and Law 7 (records of truth are permanent: a trouble raised from a red measured over a tree no commit carries is a false entry in a record of truth). Measured: 4faf4e29 staged only cairn/tools/base history.json and state.json; the reseal ran every cairn/tools/base proof over the working tree carrying 11cd's uncommitted transitions.py, ran test_transitions.py red, raised seal-red-cairn-tools-base, and left 22 base validations HELD (F17 (b)).
how: In cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py: the test stage_clean_seals already applies AFTER the run (a seal is staged only when the proof file and every file in its closure carry no unstaged change and nothing untracked) moves BEFORE the run. A proof whose closure is dirty against the index is not run: outcome 'held', no seal written, no trouble raised, the dirty paths named; the commit that carries those files reseals it. cli --reseal --stage prints HELD for it as it prints HELD today. One shared predicate, so the before-run hold and the after-run stage cannot disagree. Questions a Haiku-level builder would need, answered here: Where? cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py and cairn/devices/tester/cli.py only. (A) New module-level function dirty_against_index(proof_rel: str, closure: list[str] | None, base: Path) -> list[str], placed directly above stage_clean_seals: files = list(closure) if closure is not None else [os.path.relpath(component_root_for(str(base / proof_rel)), base)]; files.append(proof_rel); runs the same two git calls stage_clean_seals runs today (git -C base diff --name-only -- *files; git -C base ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- *files) and returns sorted(dirty + untracked). stage_clean_seals calls it in place of its inline calls; its behaviour is otherwise unchanged. (B) reseal() and reseal_all() gain keyword index_only: bool = False; reseal_all passes it through. In reseal(), directly after `if before["proven"]: return {...unchanged...}` and before the raiser is resolved: if index_only, top = subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(proof.parent),'rev-parse','--show-toplevel'], capture_output=True, text=True); if top.returncode == 0: base = Path(top.stdout.strip()); trail = read_validations(str(proof)); closure = closure_of(trail[-1]) if trail else None; dirty = dirty_against_index(os.path.relpath(proof, base), closure, base); if dirty: return {'proof': rel, 'outcome': 'held', 'rung': 1, 'ran': False, 'because': dirty, 'why': 'the commit does not carry ' + ', '.join(dirty[:3]) + ' — this proof measures what is committed, so it waits for the commit that carries them'}. (C) stage_clean_seals: at the top of its loop, a result whose outcome is 'held' appends {'validation': os.path.relpath(validations_path_for(str(base / r['proof'])), base), 'because': r['because']} to held and continues. (D) cli.py _reseal_run: door.reseal_all(..., index_only=bool(args.stage)). Proof: a new file cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_measures_what_the_commit_carries.py, teeth (1)-(4) as named in the falsifier, PROVES = {<this ticket id>: {'1': ..., '2': ..., '3': ..., '4': ...}}, main via print_teeth_main like test_reseal_stages_clean_seals.py; its fixture is test_reseal_door.py's _component()/_record()/_FakeTester/_FakeRaiser shape inside a scratch_dir that is git init'd with user.email/user.name configured, every git call -C the scratch repo, never the live tree. Its validation record cairn/devices/tester/validations/test_a_seal_measures_what_the_commit_carries.json.
falsifier: Falsifier: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_measures_what_the_commit_carries.py green and sealed under bin/cairn test --netns, teeth under PROVES for this ticket: (1) test_a_proof_whose_closure_is_dirty_against_the_index_is_held_and_never_run — a scratch git repo holding widget/code.py and widget/proofs/test_widget.py, committed, a green seal persisted over it; code.py then modified and left unstaged; reseal(proof, index_only=True, tester=<counting fake>, raiser=<recording fake>) returns outcome 'held' with 'widget/code.py' in because, the fake ran 0 times, the validations file is byte-identical before and after, and nothing was raised; (2) test_the_same_proof_runs_once_the_commit_carries_its_closure — the same fixture with code.py staged: reseal(index_only=True) runs the fake once and returns 'resealed'; (3) test_the_stage_lists_a_held_result_and_a_manual_reseal_still_runs — stage_clean_seals([<the held result>], root=repo)['held'] carries its validation path and because, and reseal(index_only=False) over the dirty fixture runs the fake once; (4) test_the_hook_path_passes_index_only — cli._reseal_run with stage=True calls reseal_all with index_only=True, and with stage=False with index_only=False (reseal_all, staged_files and proofs_touching replaced by recording stand-ins). Teeth 1 and 4 red with reseal.py and cli.py reverted to the pre-build commit (the hollow). Horizon: this voyage; then the next records-only commit over a component carrying an uncommitted build prints HELD without RED.

decisions.text: D1: the proof ALREADY LANDED in cairn commit 51c1e053 (red proof): cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_measures_what_the_commit_carries.py carries PROVES['42075a49c121'] with keys '1'-'4' naming the four teeth of the falsifier and its fixtures (_dirty_repo, _FakeTester, _FakeRaiser), all four standing red against today's code; it builds as written — the build edits NO proof file, only cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py (D2-D4) and cairn/devices/tester/cli.py (D5).

D2: reseal.py gains def dirty_against_index(proof_rel: str, closure: list[str] | None, base: Path) -> list[str], placed directly above def stage_clean_seals: files = list(closure) if closure is not None else [os.path.relpath(component_root_for(str(base / proof_rel)), base)]; files.append(proof_rel); dirty = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(base), 'diff', '--name-only', '--', *files], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split(); untracked = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(base), 'ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard', '--', *files], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split(); return sorted(dirty + untracked). stage_clean_seals replaces its own files/dirty/untracked lines with dirty = dirty_against_index(r['proof'], closure, base) and holds when dirty is non-empty; its behaviour is otherwise unchanged. os, subprocess, Path and component_root_for are already in scope in reseal.py.

D3: reseal() and reseal_all() each gain the keyword index_only: bool = False, and reseal_all passes index_only=index_only into each reseal() call. In reseal(), directly after the block 'if before["proven"]: return {... "unchanged" ...}' and before the comment that begins 'RESOLVED ONCE, HERE' (so before the raiser is resolved and before any run): if index_only: top = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(proof.parent), 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel'], capture_output=True, text=True); if top.returncode == 0: base = Path(top.stdout.strip()); trail = read_validations(str(proof)); closure = closure_of(trail[-1]) if trail else None; dirty = dirty_against_index(os.path.relpath(proof, base), closure, base); if dirty: return {'proof': rel, 'outcome': 'held', 'rung': 1, 'ran': False, 'because': dirty, 'why': 'the commit does not carry ' + ', '.join(dirty[:3]) + ' — this proof measures what is committed, so it waits for the commit that carries them'}. A proof outside any git repo (returncode != 0) runs as today.

D4: in stage_clean_seals, the FIRST statement inside the for r in results loop is: if r.get('outcome') == 'held': held.append({'validation': os.path.relpath(validations_path_for(str(base / r['proof'])), base), 'because': r['because']}); continue — before the existing outcome filter, which is otherwise unchanged.
decisions.step: the stage lists a held result

decisions.text: D5: in cairn/devices/tester/cli.py _reseal_run, the call door.reseal_all(proofs, ruling_id=args.ruling, timeout=args.timeout, skip_settled=not args.targets) gains index_only=bool(args.stage); and in its results loop, a branch elif r['outcome'] == 'held': continue is added before the final else, because a held result is printed by the existing HELD line under if args.stage (the only path that produces one) and must not also print as RESEAL.
decisions.step: the cli passes index_only and prints a hold once

decisions.text: D6: D1-D5 are this ticket's decision list, one per build step; the how field and the sorted berth's builder_check are their prose source, and where they differ the D line governs.

D7: confirmed against cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py at HEAD: lines 85-95 already import closure_of, component_root_for, read_validations and validations_path_for from cairn.tools.validation_store.validation_store, and os, subprocess and Path are imported at lines 75-79; nothing new is imported. In D3, rel is the existing local assigned at line 326 ('rel = _rel(proof)', the repo-relative proof path every reseal() return uses); the path handed to dirty_against_index is computed inline as os.path.relpath(proof, base), as D3 says. D4's validations_path_for is the same import.

D8: in stage_clean_seals, closure is the existing local, computed by lines 603-607 that D2 keeps unchanged: proof = base / r['proof']; trail = read_validations(str(proof)); if not trail: continue; closure = closure_of(trail[-1]). D2 replaces only the lines after them (608-614: the files list, the git diff call and the git ls-files call) with dirty = dirty_against_index(r['proof'], closure, base), and the hold reads 'if dirty:' in place of 'if dirty or untracked:', appending sorted dirty paths as 'because' exactly as today.
